human_readable: Market clearing prices presented as a natural law of supply and demand in housing markets
summary: KERNEL CONTEST: The commitment 'housing prices are set by a natural law of supply and demand' is held under sharply different readings. Under a naturalist reading, price formation is a mountain — an inevitable equilibrium process no one controls and no one collects from. Under an institutional reading, the clearing price is constructed by zoning, lending standards, tax treatment, and platform intermediaries, with identifiable beneficiaries (incumbent owners, lenders, intermediaries) and identifiable payers (renters, first-time buyers). The contest is whether 'the market price' names a natural fact or an enforced allocation presented as one.
